territorial_scope.description: Applies in Denmark, excluding the Faroe Islands and Greenland, and supplements the directly applicable EU AI Regulation.

evidence.quote: Loven gælder ikke for Færøerne og Grønland.

summary.short: Danish bill supplementing the EU AI Regulation (2024/1689). It designates national competent and market-surveillance authorities, gives them inspection, order, blocking and disclosure powers, requires registration of certain AI systems, and sets fines and criminal liability. Proposed entry into force 2 August 2026.
summary.long: The bill supplements Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 on AI. It has the Minister for Digitalisation set rules designating competent and market-surveillance authorities, makes the Digitaliseringsstyrelsen the central contact point and coordinator, and gives the Domstolsstyrelsen market-surveillance tasks over courts' use of AI systems. Market-surveillance authorities may request information, order warnings, remedies, withdrawal or recall of non-compliant AI systems, impose temporary bans on supply or marketing, sample systems, access premises without a court order, and publish information on non-compliant systems. Orders to owners of online interfaces may be enforced by court-ordered blocking. AI systems used as safety components in critical digital infrastructure, road traffic, or water, gas, heat and electricity supply must be registered with the Digitaliseringsstyrelsen. Fines apply to listed violations of the AI Regulation's provisions, and legal persons may face criminal liability; the limitation period is 5 years. Fines may be settled by summary penalty notice. The bill would enter into force on 2 August 2026 and does not apply to the Faroe Islands and Greenland.

thresholds.note: No numeric cutoff in this bill changes legal treatment of any person or entity. The numbers present are procedural or retention periods, not thresholds: appeal deadline of 4 weeks (§ 3, stk. 4), re-application wait of 3 months (§ 11, stk. 4), 5-year retention period (§ 5, stk. 3), 5-year limitation period (§ 17, stk. 4), and the entry-into-force date (§ 19). Fine amounts are not stated in this text. Scope-defining references to AI Act articles are not numeric thresholds.
